source.title: Towards Understanding the Role of Over-Parametrization in Generalization of Neural Networks
source.authors: Behnam Neyshabur; Zhiyuan Li; Srinadh Bhojanapalli; Yann LeCun; N. Srebro

record.file_problem: none; full paper text, including supplementary experiments, is present.
record.tranche_reason: It tests whether wider networks continue to generalize after fitting the training data, using width sweeps and test error rather than the original study's exact setup.
record.gate_note: The paper cites earlier random-label results but does not reproduce them. Figure 5 capacity-bound comparisons are not rows because they compare bounds rather than report the behavior the claim versions name.
record.test_reason: The study repeats V2's method and measure: width sweeps of one-hidden-layer ReLU networks trained with SGD without explicit regularization, measuring training and test error. CIFAR-10 and SVHN results explicitly show improvement beyond zero training error.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors propose tighter unit-wise capacity bounds that decrease with width and could explain improved generalization, and prove a matching capacity lower bound. They emphasize that the bounds remain numerically loose, their theory concerns two-layer networks, and they do not explain why optimization finds low-complexity solutions.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses two-layer fully connected ReLU networks and an SGD width sweep without weight decay or dropout; its datasets and experiment details differ from the version's cited study.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports the width-related test-error trend on CIFAR-10 and SVHN; MNIST is shown only in a figure without a prose description of its result.

fits_no_version.finding: Pre-activation ResNet18 test error decreases beyond the size needed to fit CIFAR-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing width beyond training-set interpolation can improve generalization in deep residual convolutional networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Unit capacity and unit impact decrease with width on CIFAR-10 and SVHN.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Wider two-layer networks learn smaller per-unit distances from initialization and smaller outgoing-weight magnitudes.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 4 compares normalized-margin distributions for networks trained on true and random labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed capacity measure distinguishes normalized-margin distributions under natural-label and random-label training.

record.problems: The relevant test-error curves are figures without numerical values or reported uncertainty. The text describes the trend for CIFAR-10 and SVHN, but not the MNIST error trend.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible result rows were omitted. The ResNet18 result is mentioned in fits_no_version because it is not the one-hidden-layer setting named by V2. Figure 5 capacity-bound comparisons were excluded because they do not measure the behavior named in the claim versions.

untested.parts: The study does train networks on true and random labels for Figure 4's normalized-margin comparison, contrary to the record. It does not report the paired training-fit and held-out-accuracy results needed to test V1.

The exact original downsampled CIFAR-10 setup and unrestricted convergence are not established: training stops at cross-entropy 0.01 or 1000 epochs. No interpolation-threshold test-error peak is established.
No controlled convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison or test of learned local connectivity.
No magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness measurement or ranking of generalization gaps by that measure.
No removal of memorized training examples.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source listed for V2. The MNIST result has qualitative textual support that the extraction missed. Random-label training is present, but its normalized-margin comparison does not establish V1.

versions.untested_parts: No experiment in this paper trains on random labels or compares their held-out performance with natural-label training.
The reported two-layer sweeps use CIFAR-10, SVHN and MNIST; they do not test downsampled CIFAR-10 or the exact settings of Neyshabur, Tomioka & Srebro 2015.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks on the same image task.
The paper measures unit capacity and unit impact, not magnitude-aware sharpness or the tested norm- and margin-based generalization measures in this version.
